title: Slovenia Walks a Fiscal Tightrope as Growth Optimism Meets EU Budget Scrutiny · 15 Oct
keywords: Slovenia, fiscal policy, EU budget rules, deficit, Janez Janša, IMF growth forecast, public spending, European Commission, fiscal framework, trade unions, public sector reform, inflation, cost of living, excessive deficit procedure, Slovenian economy
notes: Slovenia's government is pressing ahead with expansionary budgets for 2027 and 2028, framing higher public investment as a development strategy rather than fiscal recklessness. But a gap between Ljubljana's own deficit projections and the European Commission's earlier forecasts has handed critics a credible line of attack. The dispute goes beyond ideology: it raises pointed questions about whether the government's assumptions are robust enough to withstand a growth shortfall.
